title: Holmes the mouthpiece freak
summary: He never used the stock mouthpiece, tried every kind of metal and other mouthpiece, and sold two from a drawerful to a player from Machito's band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did you personally have a lot of fussing and doing with mouthpieces and reeds and all that? Because a lot of saxophone...
I was more like a... I was more a mouthpiece freak. You know, I've never got a decent mouthpiece. No mouthpiece ever suited me. I was more a mouthpiece freak, and he was a reed freak!
In other words, when you bought a saxophone and it came with a mouthpiece, you were never...
Oh, I was satisfied then. I was a kid then.
But I mean, later...
Later?
If you bought a new horn, did you...
Oh, no. I never used a mouthpiece that came with a horn.
No, you never did.

No. I always had a different mouthpiece. You know, a personal mouthpiece. Most of the mouthpieces that come with horns, they're for amateurs. You know what I mean? They're just what's called stock. They're in stock. No pros ever use them. They go out and buy special
Holmes (1/14) - 22
mouthpieces, and this-that-and-the-other.
For instance, if you bought a Selmer horn...
I wouldn't buy a Selmer mouthpiece.
No?
No.
Who were the mouthpiece manufacturers then?
Oh, there was millions of them. Oh, there was millions of them. Mouthpieces, that was a big thing...
Because I would figure Selmer would be one of the biggest mouthpiece makers.

No, they make the horns. They make mouthpieces, but I mean, they make the horn. There was very few really good professionals who used Selmer mouthpieces. They might use them on clarinet, clarinettists in the symphonies, things like that. But in the Jazz world. They play altogether different.
What brand did you have that you used more than anything else?
Well, the one I had that I used longer than anything was... Well, what was it? I don't know. I used it about forty years, and I can't even think of the name of it! I don't know.
Was it made by somebody like Conn or somebody like that?
Holmes (1/14) - 23
No-no, no. It was made by a mouthpiece... That's all they made, was mouthpieces.
Oh, I see.

And like I say, there's hundred of mouthpiece makers. This one I had... Well, I didn't have one; I had a whole lot of them. I was on the mouthpiece kick. Which is not a good kick to get on, because you get to changing them things and you're never satisfied. You get so no mouthpiece would satisfy you. Then you change and get another one, and it's the same thing. I did it for years...
Did you try metal mouthpieces?
I tried them all.
You tried them all.

Sure. Tried them all. And I almost had a whole drawer full of mouthpieces. And I started getting rid of them. You know, what do I want with all these mouthpieces. I started to get rid of them, and I had about seven or eight of them left, seven or eight left over. And a fellow came to the house from Machito's band, I didn't know him, and he told me that one of the fellows in the band sent him to me, said that I had... He named the type of mouthpiece he wanted, and asked me did I have one. So I told him, yes, I had quite a few of them. And it was just what he wanted! So he bought one off me. He sat here, and
Holmes (1/14) - 24

tried it and tried it and tried it for a few hours, and blew and blew and blew and blew and blew -- and he could play, too. And he played this mouthpiece over and over and over. And he liked it, and so then he bought it. And about six weeks later he comes back and wants me to sell him another one which I had -- he had tried this other one, too. So I told him, 'Have that, too.' See, I had a whole drawer full like them.
